Section 45(4) requires that where a pension does not exceed 10% it is to be paid to the worker in a lump sum unless the Board decides it would not be to the advantage of the worker to do so, in contrast to section 26 which provides the Board with a discretion whether to grant a worker's request for a commutation of his pension.  Board policy also recognizes that section 45(4) commutations will be more readily available.  But in this case, it was not to the advantage of the worker to have his pension paid in one lump sum.  It was important that the worker continue to receive a Board pension to provide an assured source of monthly income since his disability significantly affected his ability to work, his condition might deteriorate in the future, he had been unable to obtain or keep full-time employment for any length of time in the past four years, and his plans for future employment were vague.
